chapter_title: Concerning why if a [Nail] is cut the Person shall not be sick; but if a Limb is cut he shall immediately be pained.
chapter_note: This chapter is largely dialogue frame (disciple question + apostolic response formulae + closing). The only recoverable older teaching-like content is a short correspondential analogy (body↔earth; limbs↔trees; regrowth varieties) explaining why some cuttings cause pain and others do not. It stays within natural/microcosmic correspondences and does not pivot to church institutions or Gospel citation, but it lacks the distinctive systematic cosmological architecture found in the strongest CORE strata; hence it is treated as a core fragment embedded in a later instructional frame.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue frame (“Once again… questioned the apostle”). Hagiographic/compilational wrapper.
Disciple’s addressed question (“Tell me, my master…”) with physiological setup; functions as Q-frame rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.
Speech attribution (“Then the apostle speaks…”); explicit Layer-2 dialogue marker.
